Never apply here, even with `apply=True`. The no-actions path (`code_actions.py:66-72`) returns a `CodeActionResult` with `available_actions=[]`. The titled path wraps the `post_apply_diagnostics` result with `CodeActionResult.model_validate({**result.model_dump(), 'available_actions': titles})`. (3) `tool_registry.py:611-623`: change the return annotation to `CodeActionResult`, add it to the `models` import block (`tool_registry.py:49-98`), and reword the docstring: omitting `action_title` returns the available titles in `available_actions` without previewing or applying. (4) `docs/tool-reference.md:81`: set the return column to `CodeActionResult`, as the drift gate `tests/unit/test_doc_tool_count_drift.py:220-247` requires. Rejected alternatives: a description-only fix (keeps the silent first-action apply); titles packed into the `description` string (not machine-readable); an optional field on the shared `RefactorResult` (widens the output schema of about 30 tools). |

### 7. bl-0030

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Route | deepen |
| Diagnosis | Root cause: a 5 s Pyright request timeout, combined with one cold Pyright process per test. `mcp_session` in `tests/integration/conftest.py:26-94` is function-scoped, so every test spawns a fresh server and a cold `pyright-langserver`. The first semantic request (hover / rename / references) then lazily parses and binds typeshed builtins plus the fixture file. That request goes through `PyrightLSPClient._request` (`src/python_refactor_mcp/backends/pyright_lsp.py:194-217`) under `asyncio.wait_for(..., timeout=self._request_timeout_seconds)`. The budget comes from `PYRIGHT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` with a hardcoded default of `"5"` (`pyright_lsp.py:169-173`); the conftest `server_env` (`conftest.py:57-63`) never sets it. Measured this session on an idle machine: `test_get_type_info_returns_non_empty_type` call phase took 1.52 s (setup 4.52 s), which leaves about 3.3x headroom. The gate evidence shows a 2.1x average slowdown (230 s vs 108 s); per-request peaks under parallel CPU load go past 3.3x. All three failing tests go through Pyright `_request`: `get_type_info` does a hover, `rename_symbol` does a rename, and `find_constructors` calls `pyright.get_references` (`tools/search/constructors.py:125`). This matches the `PyrightError: ... timed out after 5.0s` shape. The row is confirmed; the anchors `tests/integration/test_end_to_end.py` and `scripts/test-integration.ps1` exist. The script itself is not at fault because it only sets `RUN_MCP_INTEGRATION`. |
| Approach | Add an integration-only timeout budget without loosening production. (1) In `tests/integration/conftest.py`, add `"PYRIGHT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS": os.environ.get("PYRIGHT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS", "30")` to the `server_env` dict (`conftest.py:57-63`), placed after `**os.environ` so an operator override still wins. Hoist `30` into a named module constant, e.g. `_INTEGRATION_PYRIGHT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`, with a one-line docstring comment giving the reason: a cold Pyright per test plus parallel gate load. 30 s gives about 20x headroom over the measured 1.5 s cold request, and a real hang still fails the test within a bounded time. (2) Document the timeout env vars in the `ai_docs/runtime.md` `## Config And Environment` table (`runtime.md:62-73`). `PYRIGHT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (default 5, floor 1), `JEDI_OPERATION_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (default 10) and `ROPE_OPERATION_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (default 30) are all absent today, which violates `runtime.md:107` (new env var -> add it here). Also record the root cause and the integration override in the Pyright row's note. Rejected alternatives: a session-scoped warm server would break per-test `tmp_path` isolation and the `indirect` profile parametrization; a warm-up request in the fixture only moves the cold cost into setup, which is still bounded by the same 5 s; raising the production default has no production evidence behind it (tracked as a follow-on in notes). |
| Scope | Production files: 0. Test files: 1 (`tests/integration/conftest.py`, extended; no new test methods). Doc files: 1 (`ai_docs/runtime.md`). Changelog fragment: `changelog.d/maintenance-bl-0030.md`. No deletions. Within Rule 3/4 targets; no forcing shape claimed. |
| Tool policy | edit-only |

### 9. bl-0020

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Route | deepen |
| Diagnosis | Confirmed at HEAD `80b1930`. Every tool is a plain `async def` whose signature MCPServer introspects through `tool_error_boundary`'s `__wrapped__` chain (`src/python_refactor_mcp/tool_registry.py:1-32` module docstring; registration loop `tool_registry.py:1871-1879` passes only `description=` from the docstring and `annotations=`, so nothing supplies per-parameter text). Signatures use bare types, e.g. `find_references` at `tool_registry.py:128-136` (`file_path: str`, `line: int`, ...), `apply_code_action` at `tool_registry.py:611-617`, `undo_refactoring` at `tool_registry.py:1538`. An AST sweep of both files found 109 top-level `async def`s (97 in `tool_registry.py`, 12 in `server.py`; one is `app_lifespan`, not a tool) and 7 zero-parameter tools, so 101 parameterized tools, matching the row's evidence. Live probe: `server.mcp.list_tools()` (refactoring profile, 75 tools) reports 0 tools with any described property. The single existing `Annotated` use, `index: Annotated[int, Field(ge=0)]` at `server.py:282`, already emits `minimum: 0` in the live schema. A scratch probe that wrapped a function with `FilePath = Annotated[str, Field(description=...)]` in `tool_error_boundary` got `description` in `inputSchema.properties.file_path`, under `from __future__ import annotations` plus `eval_str`. So the mechanism works end to end, and the gap is only that no parameter carries metadata. |
| Approach | (1) New module `src/python_refactor_mcp/tool_params.py` (depends only on `typing` and `pydantic`, so no import cycle) holding the single source: a `PARAM_DESCRIPTIONS: dict[str, str]` keyed by parameter name, plus `Annotated` aliases built from it, e.g. `FilePath = Annotated[str, Field(description=PARAM_DESCRIPTIONS["file_path"])]`. Aliases cover every name used by 2 or more tools. Probe counts: `file_path` 84, `apply` 44, `line` 38, `character` 38, `file_paths` 21, `limit` 14, `class_name` 8, `root_path`/`offset` 4, `start_line`/`start_character`/`end_line`/`end_character`/`source_file`/`depth`/`max_items`/`pattern` 3, then about 12 names at 2 uses. Nullable and defaulted variants get their own aliases where the base type differs (e.g. an optional `limit`). Defaults stay on the signature (`limit: OptionalLimit = DEFAULT_SEARCH_SYMBOLS_LIMIT`). (2) `src/python_refactor_mcp/tool_registry.py`: import the aliases (they must resolve in module scope for `eval_str=True`, as the module docstring requires) and retype matching parameters in the 97 delegates. Give the 6 tools with no alias-covered parameter one described parameter each: `create_type_stubs` (`package_name`), `autoimport_search` (`name`), `diff_preview` (`edits`), `refactor_transaction` (`steps`), `undo_refactoring`/`redo_refactoring` (`count`). Add these as entries in `PARAM_DESCRIPTIONS` rather than inline strings, to keep one source. (3) `src/python_refactor_mcp/server.py`: same retyping for the 12 explicit wrappers; fold the existing `Field(ge=0)` on `index` (`server.py:282`) into a described alias. Mirror `server.py:282` for the syntax. Do NOT add `Args:` sections to docstrings, and do NOT remove the enforced `POSITION_CONVENTION_PHRASE` from tool descriptions (`tests/unit/test_server.py:140-175` locks it). Parameter descriptions come from `Annotated` only. Parameter names, types, defaults and validation are unchanged, so the change is non-breaking. |
| Scope | Production files: 3. `src/python_refactor_mcp/tool_params.py` (new), `src/python_refactor_mcp/tool_registry.py`, `src/python_refactor_mcp/server.py`. Test files: 1 (extend) `tests/contract/test_mcp_protocol.py`. New tests over the union of both `TOOL_PROFILES` via the existing `_profile_tools` helper: (a) every tool with a non-empty `properties` has at least 1 property carrying `description`; (b) drift lock: every property whose name is a key of `PARAM_DESCRIPTIONS` carries a non-empty description, so a future tool typed bare `file_path: str` fails while a deliberately distinct alias (different text for a different meaning) still passes. Changelog fragment `changelog.d/added-bl-0020.md`. Within Rule 3 target. The diff is wide but uniform: about 300 one-token signature-line edits across 2 hotspot files, plus a new module of about 80 lines. The review surface is the alias module; the retyping is mechanical. It is not split, because either half alone fails contract test (a). |
| Tool policy | edit-only — the retype is a textual type-annotation edit in two files with no symbol rename, move, or cross-module reference change; `preview-then-apply` (Rule 3b) targets symbolic refactors, and the schema-diff check in Validation is the preview evidence. |
| Estimated context cost | 55000 |
| Risks | Fanout probe (shape B, per-target edit of N named things): the defining files of all 101 parameterized tools are exactly `tool_registry.py` (97 defs) and `server.py` (12 defs) per the AST sweep; with the new alias module, fanoutEstimate 3 = productionFilesTouched 3. Hotspot overlap: siblings bl-0019 (annotation records at `tool_registry.py:1697-1705`) and bl-0023 (`apply_code_action` description at `tool_registry.py:611-619`) also edit `tool_registry.py`. There is no compile dependency, so the conflict graph serializes them. If bl-0023 lands first and changes what omitting `action_title` means, then any `action_title` description written here must match it (`action_title` is a singleton, so this plan does not alias it by default). Wording: `file_path`, `limit` and `apply` mean slightly different things per tool (source file vs anchor file; result cap vs root cap). Keep alias text generic and true for every use. Before writing the path text, check it against the `PATH_PARAMS` resolution rules in `tool_runtime.py`. A tool whose meaning differs gets a distinct alias, not a misleading shared one. Coverage choice: about 50 single-use parameter names stay undescribed outside the 6 uncovered tools. Acceptance requires at least 1 described parameter per tool; describing every one of 83 distinct names roughly doubles the diff for marginal value. Do not strip existing docstring guidance about parameters: removing it is out of scope, and `test_server.py:140-175` enforces the position phrase. Optional alias shapes (`X | None = None`) must keep their `null` default, or the `default == 200/500` assertions in `test_workspace_scale_tools_advertise_default_bounds` (`test_mcp_protocol.py:167-188`) drift. |
| Validation | `.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m pyright src/python_refactor_mcp/tool_params.py src/python_refactor_mcp/tool_registry.py src/python_refactor_mcp/server.py`; `.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m pytest tests/contract/test_mcp_protocol.py tests/unit/test_server.py -q`. Repro before and after: count the tools in `server.mcp.list_tools()` for each profile that have a described property; it must go from 0 to every parameterized tool. Diff every tool's `inputSchema` before and after with `description` keys stripped; it must be byte-identical, which proves there is no type, default or `required` drift. Final: `just ci` with `CHANGELOG_BASE_REF=<baseRef>`. |
